newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Moskow says 1997 US GDP to avg near 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Moskow says 1997 US GDP to avg near 2.5 pct.

text.p: Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Michael Moskow said on Thursday that he expects real U.S. 1997 Gross Domestic Product growth to reach the high end of the Chicago Fed's forecasted 2.0 to 2.5 percent range, citing a strong first quarter.
"I'd expect the higher end of that range. The first quarter seems to be coming in at strong levels," Moskow said, speaking to reporters after a speech in Dana Point, California.
"For the full year we are going to average about 2.5 percent," he added.

Regarding economic growth in the first quarter of this year, Moskow said: "When you put a number of factors together, I think you will see the first quarter coming in above that (2.0 to 2.5 percent GDP) range."
He cited employment growth, total hours worked, and consumer spending as the relevant factors.
Moskow also said the Chicago Fed expects U.S. core consumer inflation to grow 3.0 percent in 1997 versus last year's 2.6 percent.
